analysis.title: Under pressure (Across the Americas)
key_insights: Fed communication remains hawkish, with recent remarks focused on the size of a potential December rate hike. Waller continues to advocate a 50 bps hike in December. NY Fed's Williams said the situation does not call for dramatic action.

October FOMC minutes showed a pause to gather information. Almost all participants judged further rate increases would likely be appropriate, and a couple said a hike larger than 25 bp could be considered if inflation data were unfavorable. The minutes predate the October CPI, which came in slightly above expectations with core at 0.3% for a third consecutive month.
St. Louis Fed's Musalem said the economy will likely require several rate increases before spring 2027. Logan and Hammack last week supported raising rates in small increments.

October retail sales rose 0.2% m/m (prior 0.8%) but beat expectations. Ex-autos +0.6% (exp. 0.4%), ex-autos and gas +0.5% (exp. 0.3%), control group +0.6% (exp. 0.3%). Autos and parts fell 1.6% and furniture stores fell 1.3%.

Next week's focus is October PCE (Wednesday), with Conference Board Consumer Confidence on Tuesday and the Beige Book on Wednesday. Consensus is headline PCE +0.3% m/m (3.8% y/y) and core +0.3% m/m (3.2% y/y).

Natixis sees 10-year Treasury yields in a 4.90%-5.25% range between now and the December FOMC, currently near the low end. It stays cautiously on the sidelines and prefers waiting for 5.20%-5.25% before enacting longs.

Equity weakness is the main driver of the rates rally. Natixis sees little other catalyst for a durable rally, and a 'recession-esque' flattening is its view for next year if the Fed tightens into weaker risk markets.
An estimated ~$155mm/01 of unhedged liabilities in the 5y15y part of the curve, tied to AI-related financing, may need hedging and could limit any rally absent real signs of economic weakness.
Natixis recommends scaling into long 10yr swap spreads (wideners) at -42.5bps and -45bps, first target -35bps, stop on close under -47bps. Carry is about +1.5bps/3m. Main risk is risk assets.

Natixis estimates 10yr swap spreads were about 12bps wider in 2026 due to the AI buildout, with about $320mm/01 of paying from AI-related loan hedging. It expects spreads to narrow toward the old trend in 1Q27 as AI buildout activity slows.

September TIC data: total foreign UST holdings fell $75bn, with official holdings down $81bn and private up $5.4bn. Official holdings are 11.5% and private 17.5% of marketable debt. Japan was $1.063tn (-$5.2bn), China $563bn (-$26.8bn), and China+Belgium+Luxembourg -$12.6bn.

Brazil: the BRL is depreciating significantly more than other EM currencies on fiscal risks. Natixis sees room for further depreciation unless authorities announce a stronger commitment to fiscal responsibility.

Chile: Q3 GDP fell 1.8% q/q sa (exp. -1.4%), -1.1% y/y. All major demand components contracted. Natixis forecasts 2026 GDP of -0.75% to -0.25%, a rebound to about 2.0% in 2027, year-end inflation of 4.8-5.0% y/y, and the policy rate unchanged at 4.50% through 1H27.
